evidence: Pairwise review of all 54 scored criteria (functional 44, polish 5, visual 5) plus the 2 gates. Strengths: ownership is explicitly partitioned wherever overlap was likely: hro_job_open ('graded only in hro_interview_full and the manager rows'); hro_arrive_bottom ('Arrival of several cards together belongs to hro_bulk_move'); hro_interview_full ('Overfill by a multi-card move belongs to hro_bulk_places and by undo to hro_undo_full'); hro_refusal_status (status only, an accepted replay is 'deducted only in its own row'; anonymous 401 owned solely by hro_anonymous; Noor's not-found owned by hro_thread_access); hro_undo_restores ('The A2 undo in B(12) is graded only in hro_undo_conflict'); hro_drafts vs hro_msg_compose (clearing after send owned by compose); hro_candidate_view / hro_candidate_private / hro_candidate_linked ('This row alone owns that link', with the T-protocol substitution of the seeded Data Analyst conversation); hro_activity vs hro_activity_refusals; hro_pol_live_thread vs hro_unread_scrolled_up ('where the view goes while reading earlier messages is graded in Functional'); hro_pol_failed_send ('Unsaved note drafts are graded only in hro_pol_session_resume'). Colderwater lesson 16 (restart double penalty) does NOT recur: hro_restart compares jobs, order, notes, messages, unread counts and activity with the protocol-D before-restart record (functional prompt.md line 59), so a wrong pre-restart count is not re-deducted. No pair demands incompatible products. Checked: unread clears on open vs scrolled-up stays unread; compose box empty after send vs failed send keeps text; drafts persist vs sent text not reappearing; refused_put_back focus on the card vs pol_live_board focus kept in the note; undo-once vs earlier move no longer undoable (hireops_rules.md Undo); 'sending counts as reading' vs Mei's unread formula. All are consistent with hireops_rules.md. The prompt rule 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row' (functional prompt.md line 31; polish line 24; visual line 14) and the re-setup rule (functional line 13) mitigate most precondition cascades. DEFECT (lesson-16 pattern in different rows): the role-refusal rows make the success of OTHER rows' staff features an explicit failure condition. hro_candidate_no_staff (functional judge.toml line 184): 'Rafael's identical move, multi-card move, reject, undo, add-candidate, open-job and note requests succeed (the same-kind control) ... Fails if any replay is accepted or changes anything, or the staff control did not succeed.' hro_observer_readonly (line 175): 'Rafael's identical successful requests are the control.' hro_anonymous (line 193): 'A signed-in success of each is the control.' With prompt line 13 ('Every refusal row needs its own positive control'), a dead staff feature (undo, multi-card move or note save) is deducted in its own rows AND zeroes every role row that bundles that request type, even when every role refusal was observed correctly with the right status. This contradicts prompt line 31 and REVIEW_POLICY ('Preserve valid observations rather than inheriting a sibling verdict'), so the judge gets conflicting instructions and the outcome is undetermined. Secondary notes (accepted, not defects): (a) hro_mgr_early_refused uses 'their late-stage moves are the control' (line 157), so a blanket manager deny fails both manager rows; this is the row-30 positive control, and a blanket deny does not implement the late/early rule. (b) hro_refused_put_back needs a real refusal, so an app with no Interview limit fails hro_interview_full and also shows no reason; a vacuous pass would breach row 30, and UI-only versus server-only implementations still split the two rows. (c) hro_pol_live_board and hro_pol_live_thread are 0 when no live update arrives (polish judge.toml lines 25 and 34) while hro_live_board / hro_msg_exchange also fail; preservation cannot be shown without an update, so this is an accepted precondition. (d) hro_thread_access (Noor's send 'as not found') and hro_candidate_private (Tomas's read 'answered as not found') both test the 404-for-not-theirs rule (hireops_rules.md section 1) on different endpoints and candidates; distinct observables, Note. (e) Visual hro_vis_type anchor 5 'deliberate hierarchy' overlaps hro_vis_hierarchy, and readability appears in both vis_type and vis_color; mitigated by visual prompt line 14; P3 Note. (f) hro_gate_shared vs hro_add_candidate: gates are zero-weight all_pass, not double scoring. No configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Full configured grading/workload ... absent'), so how the judge resolves the line 13 / line 31 conflict is unmeasured.
counterexample: Broken app: everything correct except undo (the undo request returns 500, or the undo control does nothing, for everyone). Observer, Tomas and anonymous replays of move, multi-card move, reject, undo, add-candidate, open-job and note are all correctly refused (403, 403/404, 401) with nothing changed. Expected: deductions only in the undo-owning rows (hro_undo_restores 2, hro_undo_conflict 2, hro_undo_once 1, hro_undo_full 1, plus the undo legs of hro_reject_reason and hro_reopen). Actual per criterion text: hro_candidate_no_staff fails explicitly ('the staff control did not succeed'), and hro_observer_readonly and hro_anonymous lose their undo control and fail under prompt line 13, an extra 3.5 of 61 functional weight (about 3.4% of total reward) for the same defect, while prompt line 31 says the opposite. The same applies to a dead multi-card move or a dead note save.
suggested_fix: In hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff and hro_anonymous, require the staff control per request type and state that a type whose staff request never succeeded is left out of this row (scored elsewhere), with the row 0 only if no type has a successful control; delete 'or the staff control did not succeed' from hro_candidate_no_staff.
